subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: Should OpenClaw accept a narrow positive-delivery fix that relies on patched Codex PreToolUse emission and routes policy-active Codex turns through unified_exec, or should the security boundary use a broader fail-closed/native-surface-disable strategy instead?
rationale: The code repair can be mechanical, but the runtime prerequisite and compatibility/security boundary choice affects existing policy-active Codex users and cannot be settled by tests alone.

options.title: Repair then review narrow path
options.body: Require the code_mode_exec-to-exec policy repair first, then keep the PR draft until an owner accepts the patched Codex/unified_exec/runtime tradeoff.

options.title: Adopt broader fail-closed path
options.body: Prefer the fail-closed or native-surface-disable approach from the related draft PRs if positive delivery is not enough as the security boundary.

options.title: Pause until Codex ships prerequisite
options.body: Hold this PR until the required Codex hook emission behavior is available in the packaged runtime OpenClaw will ship against.

recommendation.title: Repair then review narrow path
recommendation.body: Require the code_mode_exec-to-exec policy repair first, then keep the PR draft until an owner accepts the patched Codex/unified_exec/runtime tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant has the strongest feature-history signal on Codex native tool policy and relay lifetime behavior.
